detail.longDescription: I have this attr class: import attr @attr.s class Foo: a = attr.ib() # type: int f = Foo(1, 2) I have latest Pyright and Python 3.10. Pyright warns Error: Expected 0 positional arguments in the line Foo(1, 2) . Therefore, I added a type-checking-only __init__ : @attr.s class Foo: a = attr.ib() # type: int if TYPE_CHECKING: def __init__(self, a: int): ... reveal_type(Foo.a) # Type of "Foo.a" is "int" Warning disappears, and Foo.a is correctly typed as int . Hooray. Now, I realised there is another way of writing the class (by removing the type comment and assigning a to self ): @attr.s class Foo: a = attr.ib() if TYPE_CHECKING: def __init__(self, a: int): self.a = a reveal_type(Foo.a) # Type of "Foo.a" is "Any | int" Warning also disappears. But Foo.a is now typed as Any | int . Where did the Any come from? Edit : since attr.ib() returns Any , I tried replacing the assignment with a manual annotation: @attr.s class Foo: a: Any # instead of attr.ib() if TYPE_CHECKING: def __init__(self, a: int): self.a = a reveal_type(Foo.a) # Type of "Foo.a" is "Any" But the type is now Any . int is completely erased.
